pages.note: Fetched OK; search shows current canonical path is https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/using-oauth-apps/authorizing-oauth-apps (S2 URL may redirect).

claims.claim: Registration is a settings form; OAuth App access restrictions on by default for new orgs; owner may need to approve
claims.quote: When you create a new organization, OAuth app access restrictions are enabled by default.
claims.correction: 'No GitHub review' is an absence claim; pages read describe none.

claims.claim: No GitHub review described; no org-owner turnaround stated
claims.quote: Users can request owner approval for OAuth apps they'd like to use.
claims.correction: Absence claim: no turnaround time found on the page (paraphrase-level check).

claims.claim: Account owner: personal account or org where you are admin
claims.quote: under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to.
claims.correction: For GitHub Apps the page says 'under any organization you own' (or one that granted app-management permission): slightly narrower.

claims.claim: GitHub Apps not subject to org application policies; OAuth Apps need owner authorization when policy active
claims.quote: GitHub Apps aren't subject to organization application policies.
claims.correction: Second half: 'If an organization application policy is active, only an organization owner can authorize the installation of an OAuth app.'

claims.claim: At least one callback URL, up to 10
claims.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.
claims.correction: 'At least one' is implied by the form, not quoted.

claims.claim: GitHub Apps fine-grained permissions, not subject to org policies; OAuth Apps use scopes and share user's access
claims.quote: GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions.
claims.correction: 'Share the authorizing user's access' is paraphrase of: 'Authorizing an OAuth app grants the app access to the user's accessible resources.'

claims.claim: Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps > New OAuth App; GitHub Apps path analogous
claims.quote: In the left sidebar, click Developer settings. ... In the left sidebar, click OAuth apps. ... Click New OAuth App.
claims.correction: GitHub App path (Developer settings > GitHub Apps > New GitHub App) confirmed on registering-a-github-app page.

claims.claim: Name, homepage, description, callback; Add callback URL, max 10
claims.quote: To add additional callback URLs, click Add callback URL.
claims.correction: Field list (name/homepage/description) paraphrase only.

claims.claim: Expire user access tokens on by default; uncheck only if no refresh support; Device Flow for headless/CLI
claims.quote: "Expire user access tokens" is enabled by default. Uncheck it if your app doesn't yet support short-lived tokens.
claims.correction: Device flow headless quote: 'The device flow allows you to authorize users for a headless application, such as a CLI tool.' (authorizing-oauth-apps).

claims.claim: Keep client ID/secret in server-side env vars, never frontend/git
claims.correction: Neither the creating-an-oauth-app nor authorizing page gives client secret storage guidance (the latter only describes the parameter). Good practice, but not officially stated on pages read.

claims.claim: Authorize endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, random state, PKCE
claims.quote: An unguessable random string. It is used to protect against cross-site request forgery attacks.
claims.correction: PKCE: code_challenge + code_challenge_method must be S256 ('the plain code challenge method is not supported'); table marks them strongly recommended (not required). redirect_uri is optional: 'If left out, GitHub will redirect users to the first callback URL.' Guide should mention S256 only and that PKCE is recommended.

claims.claim: Code expires in 10 minutes; exchange at /login/oauth/access_token
claims.quote: The temporary code will expire after 10 minutes.
claims.correction: Endpoint: POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token.

claims.claim: Test with own account then restricted org; no dedicated test procedure
claims.correction: Remains unverified, as the guide says; no official test procedure found.

claims.claim: Up to 10 callback URLs
claims.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.

claims.claim: Exact match by default; wildcard per URL (host+port exact, path subdirectory), security warning
claims.quote: When wildcard matching is disabled, the redirect URL must exactly match the callback URL.
claims.correction: Wildcard detail quote (about-the-user-authorization-callback-url): 'the redirect URL's host (excluding subdomains) and port must exactly match the callback URL' and 'path must reference a subdirectory'. Note host EXCLUDES subdomains, so any subdomain matches; guide wording 'host must match exactly' is imprecise.

claims.claim: GitHub Apps with single callback URL before Aug 3, 2026 have wildcard enabled
claims.quote: Apps that had a single callback URL enabled prior to August 3, 2026 have wildcard matching enabled for that callback URL.
claims.correction: Date confirmed. Imprecision: the same sentence also appears on the OAuth apps authorizing page, so it is not limited to GitHub Apps; page also recommends disabling wildcard if not needed. (Correct URL: .../registering-a-github-app/about-the-user-authorization-callback-url.)

claims.claim: Native desktop: port need not match; prefer 127.0.0.1 or ::1
claims.quote: The redirect_uri does not need to match the port specified in the callback URL for the app.
claims.correction: U() can become verified. Also: 'instead to use loopback literal 127.0.0.1 or IPv6 ::1.' Loopback example uses plain http.

claims.claim: HTTPS not stated as requirement
claims.correction: Absence confirmed: no HTTPS requirement on page; loopback example uses http://127.0.0.1:1234/path. Paraphrase-level.

claims.claim: repo: full access to public/private repos plus org-owned projects, invitations, team memberships, webhooks
claims.quote: Grants full access to public and private repositories including read and write access to code
claims.correction: Org note: 'the repo scope also grants access to manage organization-owned resources including projects, invitations, team memberships and webhooks.' Also grants managing user-owned projects.

claims.claim: read:user, user:email, read:org, workflow
claims.quote: Grants the ability to add and update GitHub Actions workflow files.
claims.correction: read:user 'Grants access to read a user's profile data.'; user:email 'Grants read access to a user's email addresses.'; read:org 'Read-only access to organization membership, organization projects, and team membership.' (also covers org projects, guide omits).

claims.claim: GitHub Apps use permissions: Read-only/Read & write/No access; webhook events depend on permissions
claims.quote: The permissions that you selected in the previous step determine what webhook events are available.
claims.correction: Dropdown choices 'Read-only', 'Read & write', 'No access'; page advises fewest permissions (paraphrase).

claims.claim: Device flow for headless/CLI; non-web PAT flow for limited situations like testing
claims.quote: Non-web authentication is available for limited situations like testing.
claims.correction: Device flow quote: 'The device flow allows you to authorize users for a headless application, such as a CLI tool.'

claims.claim: Revoke app from settings to repeat consent screen
claims.correction: Page says users can review and revoke authorizations, but not that this repeats the consent screen. Remains unverified.

claims.claim: Restrictions default-on for new orgs; members request approval; owners notified; only owner can authorize when policy active
claims.quote: When you create a new organization, OAuth app access restrictions are enabled by default.
claims.correction: 'Owners are notified' is paraphrase only on S7. 'Only owner can authorize' is quoted on S6: 'If an organization application policy is active, only an organization owner can authorize the installation of an OAuth app.'

claims.claim: GitHub Apps not subject to org policies; owner grants repo access
claims.quote: A GitHub App only has access to the repositories an organization owner has granted.
claims.correction: First half: 'GitHub Apps aren't subject to organization application policies.'

claims.claim: Org blocks unapproved OAuth App; ask owner or switch to GitHub App
claims.quote: If an organization application policy is active, only an organization owner can authorize the installation of an OAuth app.
claims.correction: 'Unapproved app cannot access org resources': paraphrase of S7 (members/outside collaborators cannot authorize OAuth app access to org resources).

claims.claim: Expiring tokens: access 8h, refresh 6 months without use; enabling doesn't expire existing; bad_refresh_token
claims.quote: The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.
claims.correction: 'Enabling this feature does not cause existing tokens to expire' and bad_refresh_token error also on page.

claims.claim: Auth code expires 10 min; device codes 900 s
claims.quote: The default is 900 seconds or 15 minutes.
claims.correction: Code: 'The temporary code will expire after 10 minutes.'

claims.claim: Up to 100 OAuth Apps per owner; 10 callback URLs
claims.quote: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.

claims.claim: Ten tokens per hour per user/app/scope
claims.quote: There is a limit of ten tokens that are issued per user/application/scope combination
claims.correction: Official: ten-token limit per user/application/scope combination (not clearly 'per hour'); a separate 'rate limit of ten tokens created per hour' is also reported by the fetch (paraphrase-level). The rate-limits page says: 'ten token limit' is distinct from the sign-in limit (ten sign-ins in one hour then re-authorization). Can be upgraded from unverified, wording tightened.

claims.claim: OAuth App tokens share user's 5,000 requests/hour
claims.correction: Not stated on the OAuth rate-limits page (it defers to REST/GraphQL rate-limit pages; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api was not fetched). Keep unverified or fetch that page.

claims.claim: HTTPS requirement for callback not stated
claims.correction: Absence confirmed; loopback example uses http.

missing: OAuth apps are rate limited on token generation: 'OAuth apps are subject to a rate limit of 2,000 access token requests per hour.' (https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/rate-limits-for-oauth-apps) plus sign-in limit: 10 sign-ins/hour then re-authorization.

Authorizing page: PKCE only accepts S256 ('the plain code challenge method is not supported'); code_challenge/method are strongly recommended; redirect_uri is optional and defaults to the first callback URL.

Both OAuth and GitHub App docs recommend GitHub Apps ('Consider building a GitHub App instead of an OAuth app') and users can edit scopes so the app may receive less than requested; check X-OAuth-Scopes header (scopes page).
